_doc: Which of runtime/sound.h's file-scope statics must NOT simply become per-instance context members. Consumed by the context generator; explained in docs/design/engine-context.md. THE DEFAULT IS per_instance — only exceptions are listed here, because 250+ of the 293 statics are ordinary audio state with no special handling. Line numbers are as of commit 5712334b; the generator matches on NAME, not line, so they are documentation rather than lookup keys.

shared._why: Process-global by necessity: tied to the audio hardware or to the OS. A per-instance copy would double-register a callback or duplicate a device.

sound_aw_stack.note: web-only (PLATFORM_WEB+DE_AUDIO_WORKLET): the audio worklet thread's actual stack. Not compiled in the AUv3 build

sound_aw_ctx.note: web-only: the Web Audio context handle. Not compiled in the AUv3 build

vox_cons_name.note: const char *[22] — an immutable name table. engine-statics counts it because isConst does not treat `const char *p` as const (the pointer is mutable, the strings are not); nothing writes it

harness._why: Debug/tooling only. Should not be in a shipping per-instance context at all.

wavcap_path.note: offline WAV capture, driven by the debug harness

looks_like_harness_but_is_public_api._why: THE TRAP IN THIS FILE. These sit in the debug neighbourhood, right after the WAV capture, and read as tooling — but they are shipping cart API, so they are per-instance and two instances sharing them would each see the other's audio. Classifying them as harness would have quietly removed a feature.

scope_buf.api: scope_read — studio.h:498, exported to carts via studio_tcc_symbols.h:191

rec_ring.api: record_arm/record_grab — studio.h:424-425; feeds INSTR_SAMPLE playback. A real sampler, not a debug tap

function_local._why: Declared INSIDE a function body. A `#define name (ctx->name)` cannot rewrite these — the declaration itself has to move. Only these seven exist, and one of them is load-bearing.

lfo_seed_ctr.note: A per-voice-start LCG counter whose documented purpose is to be identical run-to-run so --det renders stay byte-reproducible. Left shared, two instances interleaving note starts BOTH lose determinism. This is the exact class of bug a single-instance byte-exact gate cannot see: tools/refactor-guard.js would sit green through it.

dropped_reported.note: dedup latch for the queue-overflow warning; shared, instance B's drops silence instance A's warning

ctx_overflow_reported.note: same latch, for the cart-context log

itl.note: web-only scratch, fully overwritten before read; static only to keep it off the 8KB worklet stack. Wants a per-callback buffer, not a context field

pool_reported.note: dedup latch for the five POOL-EXHAUSTED warnings (added 2026-08-15 when those counters finally got a reader). Shared is right and harmless: worst case one instance suppresses a duplicate of another instance warning about the SAME process-wide pool, which is the truth anyway.

lazy._why: Per-instance, but large. Allocating these on demand is what takes an idle instance from ~6.2 MB to ~1-2 MB. Sizes measured from the declarations; total here is ~3.4 MB of the 6.2 MB.

grain_pool.note: 2 x GrainTank, 3s granular capture — the single biggest win

ctx_log.note: de_switch_cart config replay log — see open_questions.cart_switching

collision_waivers._why: A name the collision check flags, where the clash has been HANDLED at the source rather than by renaming. A waiver must say exactly how, and must not be used to silence a collision that is merely believed harmless — the check exists because the failure is a compile error at best and a silently rewritten field access at worst.

palette.clashes_with: a `stbi_uc *palette` parameter inside the vendored runtime/stb_image.h
palette.handled_by: studio.c wraps that one #include in `#pragma push_macro("palette") / #undef palette / … / #pragma pop_macro("palette")`, so the vendored header is compiled without our macro. Scoped to exactly that include, and only reachable in the DE_NO_RAYLIB build where stb_image is used at all.
palette.why_not_rename: our `palette` has 146 uses in studio.c and is the engine's core colour table; shielding one vendored include is a three-line change against a 146-line one.

defer._why: HELD BACK from the move until the matching open question below is answered. These are NOT per-instance state as far as anyone knows, and leaving them as file-scope statics preserves exactly today's behaviour — so deferring costs nothing and guessing could cost a silent bug. The first generated batch swept these in before this group existed, which is precisely the accident it now prevents: the generator has no opinion, so anything without a decision must be named here or it moves by default.

sound_synth_mode.question: synth_mode
sound_synth_mode.note: gates whether the PROCESS creates an audio device at all (sound_init 9164, sound_shutdown 9194). Per-instance copies of a process-level mode is incoherent however the harness-vs-shared question resolves

extin_r.question: mic_input_path
extin_r.note: consumer-side and probably per-instance, but held with the rest of the group so the ring and its two cursors are decided together

extin_on.question: mic_input_path
extin_on.note: THE dangerous one: if capture is process-wide, a per-instance copy means the capture thread reads whichever copy the linker picked and the mic is silently dead everywhere else

open_questions._why: Real forks that a measurement cannot settle. Each names what breaks if it is guessed wrong. NONE of them block the first batch of work — they are all in code paths the first pass can leave alone.

mic_input_path._status: ANSWERED 2026-08-13 by reading the code — do not re-open, and do not make these per-instance.
mic_input_path.question: In the AUv3 build, does host/mic audio arrive PER INSTANCE or from ONE process-wide capture device?
mic_input_path.answer: NEITHER, yet: the plug-in has no mic path at all. The mic host is ios/Sources/AudioEngine.swift + CanvasView.swift, which are the STANDALONE app; nothing in ios/AU/TinyjamAU.swift opens or pushes a mic. So the extin_* group is never exercised multi-instance today.
why_it_cannot_be_per_instance: We register as `aumu` (a music DEVICE / instrument). An instrument AU is a generator — the host hands it no audio, so there is no per-instance input bus to receive.
mic.h is DEVICE-FREE BY DESIGN (its own header says so): the engine never opens a capture device, each platform host pushes frames in. The engine could not open N devices even if we wanted it to.
Mic permission is granted per HOST APP, not per plug-in instance.
mic_input_path.decision: Leave all four SHARED — which is the status quo, so nothing changes. They stay in the `defer` group only so a future batch does not sweep them in by default.
mic_input_path.shape_when_it_arrives: One process-wide capture pushed to every instance: the ring and extin_w stay SHARED, extin_r becomes PER-INSTANCE (each consumes at its own rate), and extin_on becomes a REFCOUNT ('any instance wants the mic'), never a bool.
mic_input_path.hazard_if_ignored: A naive per-instance copy of extin_on means the capture thread reads whichever copy the linker picked: silently dead mic on every other instance.
mic_input_path.the_real_question_behind_it: Should the rack also PROCESS host audio (an `aufx` effect) rather than only generate? That is a product decision about what the plug-in is, not a refactor one, and it is the only thing that would create a per-instance input bus.

cart_switching.question: Can two AUv3 instances hold two DIFFERENT carts and switch independently?
cart_switching.stake: If yes, this 288 KB log is per-instance. If cart choice belongs to the umbrella app, it belongs to the shell instead.

diagnostics_definition.question: Is HARNESS defined by PURPOSE (debug-only) or by BUILD GUARD (#ifdef DE_TRACE)? These four ship unguarded and are read only by warning prints.
diagnostics_definition.decision: PER-INSTANCE (already moved). They cost a few bytes, each instance reporting its OWN dropped notes is more useful than a shared tally, and their siblings (bow_body_overflow, rvb_bus_overflow, grain_overflow) are already per-instance pool bookkeeping reset in sound_init. Revisit only if debug state should be kept out of the shipping struct on principle.

synth_mode._status: ANSWERED 2026-08-13 by reading the code — closed.
synth_mode.question: In the AUv3 build is there a device stream at all?
synth_mode.answer: No. de_init() — the platform seam the plug-in and iOS both enter — sets sound_synth_mode = true UNCONDITIONALLY (studio.c:3015) and never creates a stream; the host pulls de_audio_render on its own thread. The value is therefore a constant, identical for every instance in that build, and sound_stream is dead code there.
synth_mode.decision: Stays SHARED. Correct as-is, no per-instance copy needed.

dead_weight._why: Not worth migrating. Fix instead of moving.

sq_atk.note: named like a live parameter, but fx_set_squash unconditionally reassigns it to gate_coef(1) on every call and nothing else writes it. A constant wearing a variable's clothes — make it const rather than giving every instance a copy

studio_c._doc: studio.c's exceptions. UNLIKE sound.h, the default here is NOT 'everything moves': studio.c owns GPU handles, fonts, shaders and the harness, so a large minority is genuinely shared. Produced by three parallel read-only audits.

shared._why: Process/OS/GPU-owned. One upload, one program, one file handle serves every instance — duplicating these means N GPU allocations at best and a double-free or a handle unloaded while a sibling samples it at worst.

spritesheet.note: GPU texture. ⚠ SEE open_questions.colorkey — the cart API colorkey() UnloadTexture+LoadTextureFromImage this SHARED texture at runtime

game_font.note: GPU: each Font owns a texture; UnloadFont at 3692 is process-lifetime

custom_font.note: reads like a per-cart flag; is resource-ownership bookkeeping (was game_font LoadFont'ed → UnloadFont it). Duplicating risks a double free

shared._shader_note: A uniform LOCATION is a property of the program, never of an instance. Each *_shader_ok latch must move (or not move) with its shader or you get a shader used before compile.

blend_lut.note: HOISTED BACK OUT of DeVideo 2026-08-14 (round 2). 20,480 B = 58% of DeVideo, byte-identical in every instance: a pure function of base_palette[], which de_palette_init() fills with the same compile-time literals everywhere. palette_hex() writes only the LIVE palette[] (still per-instance), so nothing makes an instance's table differ. ⚠ MOVES BACK the day a real palette_set() lands (palette-and-color.md Layer 2)

blend_lut_ready.note: the once-per-PROCESS latch for the above — was write-only while per-instance (nothing read it); now it is what makes instances 2..N skip a ~1M-iteration build

tritex_fast_on.note: boot-only env A/B, never written after main()

restart_argv.note: the PROCESS's argv, passed to execv — an instance calling restart would execv the whole host DAW

de_drop_buf.note: OS drag-drop targets the WINDOW, not a panel

de_mic_web_scratch.note: the JS tap takes this pointer ONCE and writes it forever — address-stable process state, not copyable

fp_cache.note: GPU texture cache. ⚠ SEE open_questions.fp_cache_key — its key omits the palette

de_win_reveal_pending.note: Win32 + DE_NET_BUILD only; never compiled in the plug-in

de_inst_default.note: THE INSTANCE ITSELF. It cannot live inside the per-instance context it identifies — that is circular, and the compiler says so ('field has incomplete type struct DeInstance'). Step 3 replaces it with a heap allocation per audio unit.

de_cur.note: the _Thread_local pointer the seam sets and restores around a call. A struct member cannot have a storage class, and more importantly this is the MECHANISM that reaches the context — it can never be part of it.

de_inst_next_id.note: THE INSTANCE MACHINERY ITSELF. A per-instance instance counter is a contradiction

de_snd_pristine.note: the template snapshot de_instance_create copies from — process-wide by definition, and taken BEFORE instance 0 mutates the live templates

de_pristine_taken.note: the once-latch for the snapshot above

PAL_FS.note: GLSL source string literal; never written. Same isConst caveat as vox_cons_name

harness._why: Debug/tooling only. Several are OPEN OS FILE HANDLES — duplicating them interleaves or truncates the output.

midi_sched.note: --midi-note: the SYNTHETIC host-note schedule, parsed from argv. Harness input exactly like replay_ev next door, and process-level for the same reason argv is: the flag describes the RUN, not a rack. A run that sets one also skips midi_input_init (see there), so there is nothing per-instance to keep apart.

uiaudit_recs.note: ~312 KB — keep ONE shared buffer rather than duplicating

wav_out.note: open FILE*; keep --wav a single-instance mode

looks_like_harness_but_is_public_api._why: THE SAME TRAP AS sound.h's SCOPE RINGS. These sit in the debug-overlay neighbourhood and read as tooling, but they are shipping cart API — classifying them harness would #ifdef away a documented feature.

map_data.note: looks like immutable baked cart data; mset() writes it at runtime (5309)

sw_canvas_active.note: looks like the twin of a boot env flag; is recomputed EVERY FRAME (2593) and read as a live draw-path gate by ~25 primitives

sav_loaded.note: looks like a once-latch; is a per-file-load cache

function_local._why: Declared INSIDE a function body, so a `#define name (ctx->name)` cannot rewrite them — the declaration itself would have to move. Listed here because they are process-global state and somebody has to have decided that is fine, not because they are invisible.

bound.note: once-per-process latch for binding the six baked fonts. The Font/Image globals it fills are themselves SHARED (studio_c.shared), so the latch must be too — it is what stops each instance re-mallocing recs/glyphs over the shared slot and orphaning the last one (the leak fixed 2026-08-14).

c_valid.note: SAFE TO SHARE BY CONSTRUCTION, and do not "fix" this by duplicating 13 variables per instance — it buys nothing. It is a MEMOISATION of the visible-world AABB, and the cache KEY captures every input (cam.target/offset/rotation/zoom + the viewport, all per-instance reads). A hit therefore returns exactly what a recompute would, whoever computed it; two instances with different cameras simply miss and recompute. ⚠ Honest caveat: the key/value pair is not atomic, so two instances rendering on different threads could tear a read and get a wrong clamp box (a visual glitch, not a crash). Nothing has been seen; recorded because the memoisation argument is a SINGLE-THREADED one.

seen_real_touch.note: A fact about the DEVICE, not about an instance: "this machine has fingers, so stop synthesizing mouse-as-touch". Two plug-in instances run on the same physical hardware, so sharing is not merely tolerable here, it is MORE correct than per-instance — one rack learning the device is touch should settle it for the other too.

chunk.note: HARNESS scratch (the DE_MIC_WAV debug feed), fully overwritten before it is read. Static only to keep 8KB off the stack — the same shape as sound.h function_local.itl. Wants a per-call buffer, not a context field.

open_questions._why: studio.c's own forks. The FIRST one is not a detail — it changes what 'done' means for this file.

the_platform_seam_has_no_instance_argume.finding: The AUv3 today has ONE process-wide frame worker (TinyjamAU.swift: 'ONE worker per process, not per instance') and calls de_frame(t) with NO instance argument. The same is true of de_resize, de_copy_frame, de_set_safe_area, de_set_backing_scale, de_audio_render and de_set_save_dir.
the_platform_seam_has_no_instance_argume.consequence: Once studio.c's state is per-instance, one de_frame() per tick advances exactly ONE rack and the others FREEZE. The whole seam needs an instance handle, and the worker must iterate instances or become one worker per instance.
the_platform_seam_has_no_instance_argume.why_it_is_dangerous: A sound.h-style macro move COMPILES and passes every byte-exact gate while leaving this broken. refactor-guard runs one instance, so it cannot see it.
the_platform_seam_has_no_instance_argume.and_do_not: Resolve the context from a mutable global 'current instance' pointer. It would be written by the UI thread and read by the audio thread on every call — exactly the race the pending/seqlock machinery exists to prevent, reintroduced one level up.
the_platform_seam_has_no_instance_argume.why_thread_local_ALSO_fails_here: Unlike sound.h, the SAME instance is touched from THREE different threads (UI thread: de_resize/de_set_safe_area; frame worker: de_frame; XPC/view thread: de_copy_frame), and ONE worker thread serves MANY instances. A thread-local 'current instance' is therefore meaningless here. The seam must take an EXPLICIT handle.
the_platform_seam_has_no_instance_argume.concretely: de_copy_frame(dst, cap, &w, &h) has no instance parameter at all; its signature must change. And the reader must load de_pres_buf from the SAME context it loaded de_pres_seq from, or the seqlock is meaningless.

crash_handler_cannot_reach_a_context.severity: MUST BE DESIGNED, cannot be macro'd
crash_handler_cannot_reach_a_context.finding: crash_handler (studio.c:1828) is registered with the OS via signal(SIGSEGV/SIGFPE/SIGABRT/SIGBUS) at 3441-3445 and READS watches/watch_count (1838-1843) to dump them.
crash_handler_cannot_reach_a_context.problem: A signal handler takes no argument, so once watches is a context member the handler has no way to reach it.
crash_handler_cannot_reach_a_context.options: Keep a static 'last active instance' pointer for the handler to walk, or drop the watch dump from the crash path.

colorkey_mutates_a_shared_texture.finding: colorkey() is a CART API that does ImageCopy -> ImageColorReplace -> UnloadTexture(spritesheet) -> LoadTextureFromImage at 4309-4317 — it destroys and rebuilds the SHARED sheet texture with this cart's keyed colour.
colorkey_mutates_a_shared_texture.consequence: Two instances with different colorkey() values fight over one texture, and one calling it mid-draw frees a texture the other is sampling.
colorkey_mutates_a_shared_texture.question: Per-instance texture VARIANT (shared source Image), or move colorkey entirely onto the software path (sw_colorkey_on/sw_colorkey_rgb are already per-instance) and delete the GPU bake?

fp_cache_key_omits_the_palette.finding: fp_cache's key is (pat, c1, c0) only, but the pixels it bakes are palette[c1]/palette[c0] — and palette is per-instance.
fp_cache_key_omits_the_palette.consequence: A shared cache returns instance A's colours to instance B for the same pattern/index triple. A byte-exact gate can NEVER see this: one instance means one palette.
fp_cache_key_omits_the_palette.probably_moot: de_init hard-sets sw_canvas_enabled/sw_canvas_active true, so under DE_NO_RAYLIB rectfill() always takes the software branch and fp_texture is dead code. Confirm that before relying on it.

canvas_and_fb_dims_must_be_decided_toget.finding: de_grow_gpu (446-465) reallocates canvas/canvas_snap/blend_snap/smooth_rt driven by fb_w/fb_h.
canvas_and_fb_dims_must_be_decided_toget.consequence: If the render targets stay SHARED while fb_w/fb_h go per-instance, one instance resizing silently resizes another's canvas.
canvas_and_fb_dims_must_be_decided_toget.question: In the AUv3 (DE_NO_RAYLIB) build are these GL render targets compiled out entirely? If the plug-in only ever uses sw_cbuf they can stay shared-and-unused.

save_state_is_a_defect_today.finding: save_dir is process-wide, so N instances read and write one cart.sav / cart.kv / cart.blob. Worse, sav_data/kv_data are lazy-loaded once and written back WHOLE, so instance 2 writes its entire stale array over instance 1's file — last-writer-wins at FILE granularity, not key granularity.
save_state_is_a_defect_today.fix: save_dir + save_path's return buffer + sav_data/sav_loaded/kv_data/kv_count/kv_loaded all become per-instance, and the host calls de_set_save_dir per instance before de_init with a distinct leaf.
save_state_is_a_defect_today.beyond_the_refactor: A DAW expects instance state to travel inside the session document (AU fullState), not a side file. Per-instance save_dir is the correct immediate fix, not the final answer.

unrelated_latent_bug_found.finding: allocated once at canvas.texture.width x height x 4 and never reallocated, but a de_reflow cart can grow the canvas via de_set_canvas. After a grow, glReadPixels(0,0,w,h,...) writes past the buffer.
unrelated_latent_bug_found.note: Pre-existing, nothing to do with this refactor. Recorded so it is not lost.

shared._why: ONE CAPTURE DEVICE per process, so the capture path is process-wide on purpose (the waiver docs/design/engine-simplification.md already recorded for de_audio_input/de_mic_wanted/de_mic_set_active, now written where the tool can see it). Revisit if an instance ever needs its own mic routing.

mic_g_wanted.note: the device is opened once for the process; an instance asking for the mic asks for THE mic

mic_acc.note: the analysis accumulator for the one capture stream

mic_rec.note: 1.4 MB capture ring. ⚠ OPEN: two instances both calling mic_record_start() would fight over one buffer. Nothing does yet, and duplicating 1.4 MB per rack to fix a case nobody has hit is the wrong trade — but it is a race, not a waiver

mic_yin_d.note: pitch-detection scratch for the one stream

function_local._why: Declared inside mic_input_push. Process-wide like the rest of the mic path (one capture device); moved here from the top-level function_local group 2026-08-15, where they had been filed under sound.h scope and so read as unclassified.

shared._why: ONE VIRTUAL COREMIDI SOURCE per process (a single "dreamengine" port a DAW sees once), so what is on the WIRE is process-wide and the state tracking it should be too. The sibling midi_input.h went fully per-instance for the opposite reason: its ring cursors are single-CONSUMER, so sharing them SPLITS one keyboard between two racks.

midi_out_client.note: CoreMIDI handles for the one port. Duplicating them means K identically-named virtual sources, which engine-dylib-spike already lists as unresolved

midi_out_on.note: SHARED IS RIGHT AND SO IS THE TYPE. midi_send_note updates this table and sends the message unconditionally and together, so it mirrors the last note message put on the WIRE — which with one shared port is exactly the receivers state, whichever instance sent it. (An earlier note here claimed it should be a per-note REFCOUNT: that was wrong and would be worse — A on, B on, A off puts a note-off on the wire while a refcount would still read 1, so shutdown would release a note nobody is playing. Withdrawn 2026-08-15, see engine-simplification.md.) ⚠ The real narrow hazard is that the table write and the send are two steps, so two instances on different audio threads can interleave and leave the wire ON with the table 0.
